interface.title: CORN | Corpus-Oriented Relationship Notation
interface.field: Social science / computational text analysis (qualitative coding of relationship networks from document corpora)
interface.stage_of_work: Data annotation and coding (turning text documents into a relational network dataset), then export for network analysis
interface.what_it_is_for: Researchers query a document corpus, read each document, and code who-relates-to-whom ties with labels, exact-span or free-text evidence and attributes, then save per workspace and annotator and export the result as an edge list or JSON archive.

data.note: The built-in 'CORN Demo Project (corn-demo)' was installed from the home screen. It has 3 short documents: 1 'Community garden' (community), 2 'Transit meeting' (transport) and 3 'Research workshop' (education). The demo defines three tie types (support, opposition, mentorship) and one tie attribute, valence (positive/negative). Annotator 'alice' was used in workspace 'default'. No test files were available, so neither upload (project config, document annotation JSON) could be tried.

features.name: Exact-span evidence capture from a document viewer
features.general: Arm a capture mode for one coded item, drag-select a passage in the document, confirm it in a floating popover, and the passage text and its character offsets are stored on that item. The passage is highlighted and shows a hover summary, and it can be found again later.
features.specific: Press 'Select span from document' on a tie, drag across text in the document iframe, press 'Use selected span'. Reasoning text (span) fills in, 'Stored span: 0-30' is shown, the text gets a coloured highlight with a tooltip 'Amina → Ben / support', and 'Locate in document' outlines it.
steps: Press Select span from document on the tie (status: 'Pending span selection')
Drag across the passage in the document panel
Press Use selected span (or Dismiss) in the floating popover
Check the highlight and hover tooltip; the span offsets are stored
Press Locate in document to outline the stored span
serves_tasks: Attach the exact supporting passage as evidence
Code a second document to grow the network across the collection

features.name: Nested relationship editor (entries → typed ties with evidence)
features.general: A repeatable form for coding a relationship: name a source and a target, then add one or more typed links between them. Each link carries quoted evidence and/or a written note, and links or whole entries can be added and removed. Links without quoted evidence are flagged for review but still allowed.
features.specific: Annotation Panel: Network entry N has Source node and Target node. Tie K has Tie type (support/opposition/mentorship), Reasoning text (span) and Reasoning text (note). Buttons: Add tie, Remove tie, Add network entry, Remove network entry. A tie with a note only shows 'Needs span review'.
steps: Press Open annotation editor, then Add network entry
Type Source node and Target node
Choose Tie type and fill span and/or note reasoning
Press Add tie for another label on the same pair, or Add/Remove network entry
serves_tasks: Record a relationship between two actors
Record a second kind of relationship between the same pair, with only written reasoning

features.name: Schema-driven tie attribute editor
features.general: Each coded link has a collapsible set of attributes defined by the project's schema; open it and pick a value for each attribute from the allowed options.
features.specific: Attributes expander under a tie; the demo schema has one categorical attribute, valence (positive/negative). Attribute values are not written to the edge list CSV.
steps: Expand Attributes under the tie
Choose a value for each attribute (e.g. valence = positive)
serves_tasks: Add a free-text justification and a tie attribute

features.name: Corpus query with metadata, progress and sampling filters
features.general: Filter a document collection by a metadata field, by whether I have already coded each item, by machine-annotation coverage, by explicit IDs, or by a random sample. Run the query, look at the result table, then pick one result to open.
features.specific: Sidebar filters: Topic, Annotated by me (Not yet/Done/All), LLM coverage (All/Has runs/Not yet run; not run), Document ID, Random sample size. Then Run query, the Matching documents table (CSV download not tried) and the Open document dropdown.
steps: Set Topic / Annotated by me / LLM coverage
Optionally type Document ID(s) or a Random sample size
Press Run query
Read the Matching documents table
Choose a document in Open document
serves_tasks: List every document in the collection
Narrow documents by a metadata field
Show only items I have or haven't coded yet
Draw a random subset of documents
Go straight to a known document

features.name: Pending-changes save bar with validation
features.general: Keep edits across several documents as unsaved changes, show how many items are waiting and which ones, save them all at once, and report items that fail validation so they can be fixed and saved again.
features.specific: The sidebar shows 'N annotation(s) pending save' (it expands to list document IDs). 'Done / Save all' gives 'Saved 1 annotation(s).' plus an error per document, for example '2: Each tie must include reasoning text in either the span or note field.' 'Refresh annotations' reloads the stored annotations (not tried).
steps: Edit annotations on one or more documents
Press the pending-save counter to see document IDs
Press Done / Save all
Fix the documents named in any error and save again
serves_tasks: Review what is unsaved and commit it

features.name: Scoped network export
features.general: Choose which subset of coded data to export by source (all, human, machine, human-revised machine), then download it as a flat edge list table or as a full archive.

steps: Choose Export scope
Press Download edge list CSV
Press Download JSON archive

Press Export current document JSON
Upload a JSON file under Import document annotation JSON (not tried)

features.name: LLM prompt configuration, preview and job queueing
features.general: Set up a prompt template with placeholders, a model provider and generation settings, preview the filled-in prompt for the open document, save the prompt for the project or the document, and queue automated annotation for one document or the whole query result.
features.specific: LLM annotation tools: Prompt version, Prompt label, Annotation prompt template, Provider (fake), Model (fake-default), Temperature, Max output tokens, Supported prompt placeholders, Rendered prompt preview, Save as project…/Save as document…, Annotate current document / Annotate current query result set (3 docs). The queued job shows 'waiting for a worker'.
steps: Expand LLM annotation tools and pick a prompt version
Edit the template, provider, model, temperature and tokens
Expand Rendered prompt preview for current document
Press Annotate current document (or the query result set)
serves_tasks: Preview the instructions that would be sent to a language model for this document
Queue automated annotation of a document
